stage: the quest lifecycle policies against the reducer

result.policies_are_NOT_decorative: this is the useful answer of the stage: the reducer really reads all three. retryPolicy.mode and maximumAttempts are compared at lines 375-380 (mode none refuses a retry, mode quest restores the ORIGIN checkpoint and any other value restores the current one, and past maximumAttempts it rejects with QuestRetryExhausted); checkpointPolicy.mode drives the snapshots at lines 230, 289 and 341 (none saves nothing, objective saves on objective completion, any other value saves on stage entry); and the reducer's own validation requires all three at lines 691-693, so a missing one throws instead of being ignored
result.authored_distribution: thirteen quests in TWO configurations - eleven with retry none/maximumAttempts 1 and checkpoint objective, two with retry stage/maximumAttempts 2 and checkpoint stage - so the policy surface is used with more than one value rather than left at a single default
result.what_is_checked: every quest declares all three policies, retryPolicy and checkpointPolicy carry a mode, and a declared maximumAttempts below one is reported because the mode and the number then contradict each other: the policy promises a retry while the first attempt exhausts it
result.boundary: whether a retry really happens is a runtime question; announcing the policy is not the same as exercising it
